subject: VAPA
title: Advanced Art & Portfolio
description: An advanced studio course for seniors that builds technical mastery in drawing, painting, printmaking, mixed media, and digital/photo work, then centers on a year-long Sustained Investigation modeled on AP Art and Design. Students keep a process sketchbook, write artist statements, photograph and curate a college-ready portfolio, and mount a public senior exhibition.
framework: 2019 California Arts Standards for Public Schools – Visual Arts (High School Advanced proficiency level); 2020 California Arts Education Framework

standards.VA:Cr1.1.HSIII: Visualize and hypothesize to generate plans for ideas and directions for creating art and design that can affect social change.
standards.VA:Cr1.2.HSIII: Choose from a range of materials and methods of traditional and contemporary artistic practices, following or breaking established conventions, to plan the making of multiple works of art and design based on a theme, idea, or concept.
standards.VA:Cr2.1.HSIII: Experiment, plan, and make multiple works of art and design that explore a personally meaningful theme, idea, or concept.
standards.VA:Cr2.2.HSIII: Demonstrate understanding of the importance of balancing freedom and responsibility in the use of images, materials, tools, and equipment in the creation and circulation of creative work.
standards.VA:Cr2.3.HSIII: Demonstrate in works of art or design how visual and material culture defines, shapes, enhances, inhibits, and/or empowers people's lives.
standards.VA:Cr3.1.HSIII: Reflect on, reengage, revise, and refine works of art or design considering relevant traditional and contemporary criteria as well as personal artistic vision.
standards.VA:Pr4.1.HSIII: Critique, justify, and present choices in the process of analyzing, selecting, curating, and presenting artwork for a specific exhibit or event.
standards.VA:Pr5.1.HSIII: Investigate, compare, and contrast methods for preserving and protecting art; prepare and present artwork, including digital documentation.
standards.VA:Pr6.1.HSIII: Curate a collection of objects, artifacts, or artwork to impact the viewer's understanding of social, cultural, and/or political experiences.
standards.VA:Re7.1.HSIII: Analyze how responses to art develop over time based on knowledge of and experience with art and life.
standards.VA:Re7.2.HSIII: Determine the commonalities within a group of artists or visual images attributed to a particular type of art, timeframe, or culture.
standards.VA:Re8.1.HSIII: Analyze differing interpretations of an artwork or collection of works in order to select and defend a plausible critical analysis.
standards.VA:Re9.1.HSIII: Construct evaluations of a work of art or collection of works based on differing sets of criteria.
standards.VA:Cn10.1.HSIII: Synthesize knowledge of social, cultural, historical, and personal life with art-making approaches to create meaningful works of art or design.
standards.VA:Cn11.1.HSIII: Appraise the impact of an artist or a group of artists on the beliefs, values, and behaviors of a society.

units.title: Studio Practice and the Visual Journal
units.big_idea: Serious artists build habits: daily sketching, research, and reflection.

units.title: Advanced Observational Drawing
units.big_idea: Accurate seeing is the foundation for intentional distortion.

units.title: Painting: Color and Surface
units.big_idea: Color relationships and surface handling carry mood and meaning.

units.title: Launching the Sustained Investigation
units.big_idea: An inquiry question drives a body of work forward through practice, experimentation, and revision.

units.title: Digital, Photo, and Mixed Media
units.big_idea: New media and ethical image use expand what an artist can say.

units.title: Sustained Investigation: Production
units.big_idea: Depth comes from making many related works and letting each one inform the next.

units.title: Printmaking and Sculpture Extensions
units.big_idea: Translating an idea into multiples or three dimensions reveals new possibilities.

units.title: Portfolio Curation and Documentation
units.big_idea: How work is selected, photographed, and described shapes how it is understood.

units.title: Senior Exhibition
units.big_idea: Exhibiting art is a public conversation with a community.

units.title: Reflection and Next Steps
units.big_idea: An artist's practice continues beyond school through intention and community.

days.title: Studio setup
days.work: Organize a home studio corner with good light and storage; photograph it for your process journal.

days.title: Baseline drawing
days.work: Draw a self-portrait from a mirror in 45 minutes as a baseline to compare at year's end.

days.title: Skills inventory
days.work: Fill two sketchbook pages with quick tests of each medium you own and rate your comfort level.

days.title: Portfolio goals
days.work: Review the AP 2-D Art and Design portfolio structure and write three goals for your senior portfolio.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a half-page reflection on what kind of artist you want to be by June.

objectives: Use brainstorming methods to generate ideas

days.title: Mind map
days.work: Create a mind map around a single word (e.g., 'home') and branch to 30 visual ideas.

days.title: 20 thumbnails
days.work: Draw 20 two-inch thumbnails exploring compositions from your mind map.

days.title: Image research
days.work: Collect 10 reference images from Smithsonian Learning Lab or NGA open access that connect to your ideas.

days.title: Collage brainstorm
days.work: Make a quick magazine collage that combines unexpected images into a new idea.

days.title: Share & check
days.work: Present your three strongest ideas to a family member and record their feedback.

objectives: Analyze how contemporary artists develop ideas

days.title: Artist video
days.work: Watch an Art21 episode on a contemporary artist and take notes on their process.

days.title: Formal analysis
days.work: Write a formal analysis of one artwork (elements, principles, meaning) in 300 words.

days.title: Series thinking
days.work: Study how an artist develops a series and sketch three variations on one of your own ideas.

days.title: Mini-work
days.work: Complete a small finished drawing inspired by the artist's process, not their style.

days.title: Reflection
days.work: Reflect on how your response to the artist changed after research.

objectives: Render form with a full value range

days.title: Value scale
days.work: Make a 10-step value scale in graphite and in charcoal.

days.title: Egg study
days.work: Draw white eggs under a single lamp, identifying highlight, core shadow, reflected light, and cast shadow.

days.title: Still life
days.work: Set up a white still life (cups, fabric) and start a 3-hour chiaroscuro drawing.

days.title: Continue
days.work: Continue the still life, pushing the darkest darks and preserving highlights.

days.title: Critique
days.work: Finish and self-critique using a value checklist; photograph for your journal.

objectives: Draw interior and exterior spaces in perspective

days.title: Perspective boxes
days.work: Complete the Drawabox 250-box challenge warm-up (25 boxes today) in two-point perspective.

days.title: Interior
days.work: Draw a room in your home in one- or two-point perspective from life.

days.title: Exterior
days.work: Draw your street or a building from a dramatic three-point viewpoint.

days.title: Atmospheric perspective
days.work: Make a landscape study showing depth through value and detail changes.

days.title: Check
days.work: Select the strongest perspective piece and refine it.

objectives: Draw the figure with proportion and gesture
materials: family model or online timed-pose site

days.title: Gesture
days.work: Do 30 one-minute gesture drawings from a family model or timed online poses.

days.title: Proportion
days.work: Study figure proportions (head units) and draw three 10-minute poses.

days.title: Hands and feet
days.work: Fill a page with studies of your own hands and feet from multiple angles.

days.title: Master study
days.work: Copy a figure drawing by a master (e.g., Michelangelo, Käthe Kollwitz) from NGA open access.

days.title: Long pose
days.work: Complete a 45-minute figure drawing applying gesture and proportion.

days.title: Facial proportions
days.work: Draw a portrait using measured proportions from a family member or photo.

days.title: Expressive approaches
days.work: Study expressive portraits by artists such as Alice Neel and Kehinde Wiley; note choices of line and color.

days.title: Expressive portrait
days.work: Create a portrait that conveys mood through mark-making and composition.

days.title: Refine
days.work: Refine the portrait using feedback from a family member.

days.title: Critique
days.work: Hold a formal critique (describe, analyze, interpret, evaluate) of your unit drawings.

days.title: Color wheel
days.work: Mix a 12-step color wheel from three primaries plus white.

days.title: Value in color
days.work: Paint a grayscale and then a full-color version of the same simple object.

days.title: Temperature
days.work: Paint the same landscape twice: once warm-dominant, once cool-dominant.

days.title: Limited palette
days.work: Paint a still life with a Zorn palette (yellow ochre, red, black, white).

days.title: Check
days.work: Self-critique color studies and note what you'll apply going forward.

days.title: Underpainting
days.work: Tone a canvas and block in a still life with a monochrome underpainting.

days.title: Block-in
days.work: Block in large color shapes, focusing on value relationships.

days.title: Develop
days.work: Develop forms and edges; use glazing or impasto deliberately.

days.title: Finish
days.work: Add final details and highlights.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a reflection on your painting process and photograph the work.

days.title: California Impressionists
days.work: Study California plein air painters (e.g., Granville Redmond, Guy Rose) and compare to French Impressionists.

days.title: Morning study
days.work: Paint a 1-hour plein air study in morning light.

days.title: Afternoon study
days.work: Paint the same scene in afternoon light and compare.

days.title: Studio painting
days.work: Use your studies to begin a larger studio landscape.

days.title: Interpretation
days.work: Write two different interpretations of a California landscape painting and defend one.

days.title: Abstraction research
days.work: Compare works by Kandinsky, Helen Frankenthaler, and Mark Rothko; note how each conveys emotion without imagery.

days.title: Studies
days.work: Make four small abstract studies based on a piece of music or an emotion.

days.title: Final abstraction
days.work: Begin a larger abstract painting developed from your best study.

days.title: Finish
days.work: Complete the painting and finish your studio landscape from Week 10.

days.title: Unit critique
days.work: Hold a painting critique and select one painting for the portfolio.

objectives: Write a Sustained Investigation inquiry question

days.title: Study examples
days.work: Review three AP sample Sustained Investigations and note how each inquiry guided the work.

days.title: Brainstorm
days.work: Brainstorm 10 inquiry questions rooted in your life, culture, or community.

days.title: Narrow
days.work: Narrow to one question and write why it matters to you.

days.title: Planning
days.work: Make 15 thumbnail ideas responding to your question.

days.title: Proposal
days.work: Write a one-page proposal: inquiry, materials, artists to research, and a 15-piece plan.

objectives: Research artists connected to the inquiry

days.title: Research
days.work: Research three artists whose work connects to your inquiry and build a visual reference page for each.

days.title: Process study
days.work: Do a process study imitating one artist's technique.

days.title: Cultural connections
days.work: Research a cultural or historical tradition connected to your inquiry (e.g., Chicano muralism, Japanese woodblock).

days.title: First piece
days.work: Begin the first Sustained Investigation piece.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a process note on how research shaped your first piece.

objectives: Produce and revise early investigation works

days.title: Piece 1
days.work: Continue and complete piece 1.

days.title: Document
days.work: Photograph piece 1 and write a 100-character process caption (AP-style).

days.title: Piece 2 plan
days.work: Sketch three directions for piece 2 that push the inquiry.

days.title: Piece 2
days.work: Begin piece 2, experimenting with a new material or composition.

days.title: Mini-critique
days.work: Get feedback using criteria of skill, synthesis, and inquiry.

days.title: Finish piece 2
days.work: Complete piece 2 and document it.

days.title: Piece 3
days.work: Begin piece 3, deliberately revising something that didn't work earlier.

days.title: Continue
days.work: Continue piece 3.

days.title: Score yourself
days.work: Score your three pieces with the AP Sustained Investigation scoring guidelines.

days.title: Conference
days.work: Hold a progress conference and update your plan.

days.title: Copyright
days.work: Learn copyright, fair use, and Creative Commons; analyze two appropriation-art court cases.

days.title: Digital tools
days.work: Learn layers, masks, and brushes in Krita or Photopea through a guided exercise.

days.title: AI and art
days.work: Discuss ethical questions about AI image generation and write your personal policy.

days.title: Digital piece
days.work: Create a digital artwork related to your inquiry using only your own photos or CC0 sources.

days.title: Check
days.work: Finish and document the piece, citing any sources used.

days.title: Composition
days.work: Shoot 50 photos practicing rule of thirds, leading lines, and framing.

days.title: Light
days.work: Shoot the same subject in golden hour, midday, and window light.

days.title: Photo essay
days.work: Create a 6-image photo essay about your community's visual culture (signs, murals, advertising).

days.title: Edit
days.work: Edit and sequence the photo essay.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the photo essay with a statement on how images shape community life.

days.title: Image transfer
days.work: Practice gel-medium image transfers of your own photos onto paper and wood.

days.title: Mixed-media piece
days.work: Create a mixed-media work for your investigation combining transfer, paint, and drawing.

days.title: Finish
days.work: Complete the mixed-media piece.

days.title: Semester review
days.work: Lay out all semester work and select your top 8 pieces.

days.title: Semester critique
days.work: Write a semester self-evaluation and present your top pieces.

objectives: Revise inquiry based on S1 reflection

days.title: Revisit inquiry
days.work: Rewrite your inquiry question based on what you discovered in S1.

days.title: Plan
days.work: Plan pieces 6–15 with thumbnails and materials list.

days.title: Piece 6
days.work: Begin piece 6.

days.title: Continue
days.work: Continue piece 6.

days.title: Document
days.work: Finish and document piece 6.

days.title: Scale studies
days.work: Make one very small and one very large study of the same idea.

days.title: Piece 7
days.work: Begin piece 7 at a scale new to you.

days.title: Continue
days.work: Continue piece 7.

days.title: Finish
days.work: Finish piece 7.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Document and write how scale changed the meaning.

materials: a material you have not used (wax, thread, clay, coffee stain)

days.title: Material tests
days.work: Test a new material in five sketchbook experiments.

days.title: Piece 8
days.work: Begin piece 8 using the new material.

days.title: Continue
days.work: Continue piece 8.

days.title: Finish
days.work: Finish piece 8.

days.title: Document
days.work: Photograph and caption piece 8.

objectives: Analyze differing interpretations of your work

days.title: Viewer responses
days.work: Show your pieces to three people without explanation and record their interpretations.

days.title: Analysis
days.work: Compare viewers' interpretations with your intent and decide which readings to strengthen.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise one earlier piece based on critique.

days.title: Piece 9
days.work: Begin piece 9.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a process reflection on the critique.

objectives: Deepen synthesis of ideas and materials

days.title: Finish piece 9
days.work: Complete piece 9.

days.title: Art and society
days.work: Research an artist or movement that changed public beliefs (e.g., the Chicano mural movement, Faith Ringgold) and note strategies.

days.title: Piece 10
days.work: Begin piece 10, aimed at a social or community message.

days.title: Continue
days.work: Continue piece 10.

days.title: Document
days.work: Finish and document pieces 9–10.

days.title: Piece 11
days.work: Begin and work on piece 11.

days.title: Continue
days.work: Finish piece 11.

days.title: Piece 12
days.work: Begin piece 12.

days.title: Continue
days.work: Continue piece 12.

days.title: Document
days.work: Finish piece 12 and document both.

objectives: Complete the Sustained Investigation body of work

days.title: Gap analysis
days.work: Lay out all pieces and identify gaps in the investigation.

days.title: Final pieces
days.work: Create or revise pieces to fill the gaps.

days.title: Continue
days.work: Continue final pieces.

days.title: Finish
days.work: Finish the body of work (12–15 pieces).

days.title: Final critique
days.work: Hold a full critique of the investigation and score it with the AP guidelines.

objectives: Carve and print a relief block

days.title: Printmaking history
days.work: Study Japanese ukiyo-e and José Guadalupe Posada's prints; note how printmaking spreads ideas.

days.title: Design
days.work: Design a block related to your investigation, reversing the image.

days.title: Carve
days.work: Carve the block safely, testing proofs as you go.

days.title: Print
days.work: Print an edition of five with consistent registration.

days.title: Sign
days.work: Sign and number prints properly and evaluate the edition.

objectives: Translate an idea into three dimensions

days.title: Assemblage artists
days.work: Study Betye Saar's assemblages and Louise Nevelson; note how found objects carry meaning.

days.title: Maquette
days.work: Build a small cardboard or clay maquette.

days.title: Build
days.work: Build the sculpture with an armature or assemblage.

days.title: Finish
days.work: Finish surfaces and paint or patina.

days.title: Photograph
days.work: Photograph the sculpture from four angles.

days.title: Public art
days.work: Study California public art (e.g., Judy Baca's Great Wall of Los Angeles) and its community process.

days.title: Site
days.work: Photograph a local site and analyze its audience and context.

days.title: Design
days.work: Design a mural or installation for the site with a scaled rendering.

days.title: Proposal
days.work: Write a proposal with budget, materials, and community benefit.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the proposal as if to a city arts commission.

days.title: Setup
days.work: Set up even lighting with two lamps at 45° and a neutral backdrop.

days.title: Shoot 2-D
days.work: Photograph all 2-D works square to the camera, correcting glare and keystoning.

days.title: Shoot 3-D
days.work: Photograph 3-D works with multiple views and a detail shot.

days.title: Edit
days.work: Crop, color-correct, and export images at portfolio specs (e.g., 1200–2000 px).

days.title: Archive
days.work: Create an organized digital archive with titles, media, dimensions, and dates.

objectives: Curate a portfolio for a specific audience

days.title: Criteria
days.work: Write selection criteria for a college art portfolio and for a general exhibition.

days.title: Select
days.work: Select 15–20 pieces for a college portfolio and 5 for AP-style Selected Works.

days.title: Sequence
days.work: Sequence the portfolio with printed thumbnails and justify the order.

days.title: Feedback
days.work: Get feedback from an art teacher, artist, or National Portfolio Day reviewer if available.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise selection based on feedback.

materials: free portfolio site (Google Sites, Adobe Portfolio)

days.title: Statement draft
days.work: Draft a 200-word artist statement about your inquiry and process.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise the statement for clarity, removing jargon; read it aloud.

days.title: Captions
days.work: Write captions for each piece (title, media, size, year, short note).

days.title: Build site
days.work: Build an online portfolio site with gallery, statement, and contact info.

days.title: Publish
days.work: Publish the site and test it on phone and computer.

days.title: Venue
days.work: Secure a venue (library community room, co-op, café) and set a date.

days.title: Theme
days.work: Choose an exhibition title and theme that frames the viewer's understanding.

days.title: Layout
days.work: Draw an installation plan placing each work on the walls.

days.title: Labels
days.work: Write and print wall labels and an exhibition intro panel.

days.title: Promotion
days.work: Design a flyer and invitation and send them out.

objectives: Prepare art for display and preservation

days.title: Preservation
days.work: Research archival practices (acid-free materials, UV light, humidity) and compare methods.

days.title: Mat and frame
days.work: Mat and/or frame 2-D works.

days.title: Hardware
days.work: Attach hanging hardware and prepare pedestals for 3-D works.

days.title: Mock hang
days.work: Do a mock hang at home to check spacing and sightlines.

days.title: Checklist
days.work: Complete an exhibition checklist and transport plan.

days.title: Install
days.work: Install the exhibition, level and light the works, and place labels.

days.title: Artist talk prep
days.work: Prepare a 5-minute artist talk.

days.title: Opening
days.work: Host the opening reception and give your artist talk.

days.title: Feedback
days.work: Review guest-book comments and visitor conversations.

days.title: Deinstall
days.work: Deinstall carefully and write an exhibition report.

objectives: Analyze how your art and responses changed

days.title: Final self-portrait
days.work: Draw a new 45-minute self-portrait and compare it with Week 1.

days.title: Growth analysis
days.work: Write a growth analysis comparing early and late work with specific evidence.

days.title: Evaluate with two lenses
days.work: Evaluate your investigation with two different criteria sets (technical and conceptual).

days.title: Peer/mentor talk
days.work: Discuss your year with an artist mentor or teacher.

days.title: Final reflection
days.work: Write a final reflection on your artistic identity.

days.title: Art careers
days.work: Research five art careers (illustrator, art therapist, UX designer, conservator, teacher) and their pathways.

days.title: Community
days.work: Find local open studios, life-drawing groups, or community-college art classes.

days.title: Summer project
days.work: Plan a summer art project with goals and a schedule.

days.title: Final piece
days.work: Create a final sketchbook spread summarizing your year.

days.title: Portfolio conference
days.work: Present your final portfolio and plan in a conference.
